title: Checkmate in one move

D0.outcome: Says that checkmate is a check from which there is no escape, and that it ends the game.

D1.outcome: When told 'mate in one', finds the mating move (every one, if there are several) in simple positions: back rank, queen next to the king, rook on the edge.

D2.outcome: In mixed positions decides whether a mate in one exists, finds it when it does, and says 'none' when it does not.

D3.outcome: Finds mates in one that need a closer look (a discovered check, a promotion, a smothered king) by testing each check for escape, capture and block.

misconceptions: Any check the king can escape from is mate.
A check that the enemy can answer by capturing the checking piece is mate.
You need the queen to give mate.
conditions: A check is mate when the king has no free square, the checking piece cannot be captured, and the line cannot be blocked.
Before playing a check, test the three escapes one at a time: king move, capture, block.
contrasts: A check that leaves the king a free square (a luft) is not mate even when it looks like a back-rank mate.
Pieces far from the king and from the checking line do not change whether it is mate.
